answers.primary: A PostToolUse command hook in the repo's .claude/settings.json with matcher "Edit|Write" and an if condition of "Edit(*.ts)"; the script reads tool_input.file_path from the stdin JSON and runs the formatter on that file after every modification.
answers.rejected_alternative: CLAUDE.md project guidance, which is what was already tried: the model owns compliance there and skips the step probabilistically, which is exactly the observed failure.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness: the hook fires deterministically on every matching tool call regardless of whether the model remembers the instruction.
answers.context_boundary: The hook runs as a separate shell process outside the model's context window; the tool-call JSON crosses in via stdin, and only optional stdout or systemMessage feedback crosses back into the conversation.
answers.lifecycle: Fires after every successful Edit or Write tool call for as long as the settings entry exists (settings are live-reloaded); it stops applying when the entry is removed or disableAllHooks is set.
answers.failure_mode: Advisory and fails open: a formatter crash or nonzero exit is a non-blocking error so the turn continues and unformatted code can still land; it also misses files changed through raw Bash commands like sed, so a pre-commit check remains a useful backstop.
answers.version_caveat: No meaningful version gate for PostToolUse itself; comma-separated matcher lists need v2.1.191+ (the pipe form works everywhere), and single-segment if patterns like Edit(src/**) anchor to the working directory only from v2.1.214.

answers.primary: permissions.deny rules in the checked-in project .claude/settings.json: Read(.env), Read(.env.*), Read(secrets/**), plus matching Edit deny rules for the write side; deny rules only restrict, so they apply to every teammate automatically without the workspace-trust dialog.
answers.rejected_alternative: A PreToolUse hook that inspects paths and denies: permission rules are the first-class declarative fail-closed mechanism, and hooks should be reserved for logic the rule syntax cannot express.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness: the permission engine evaluates deny rules first, and prompt or CLAUDE.md text cannot change what Claude Code allows.
answers.context_boundary: Enforced at the tool-call boundary in the main session and in subagents alike; denied file content never enters any context window.
answers.lifecycle: Loaded from project settings at session start and live-reloaded on change; applies to every session anywhere in the repo until the rules are edited out.
answers.failure_mode: Fails closed for built-in tools (Read, Grep, Glob, @-mentions, and recognized Bash file commands like cat and sed) but does not bind arbitrary subprocesses: a Python or Node script the agent launches can still open the files, so pair with sandbox filesystem.denyRead for OS-level coverage.
answers.version_caveat: A Read deny rule also blocking the Edit tool on the same path requires v2.1.208+; Write and NotebookEdit path rules are never consulted (v2.1.210+ warns at startup), so the write-side rules must be written as Edit(...).

answers.primary: A Notification command hook in each engineer's ~/.claude/settings.json with matchers permission_prompt and idle_prompt, whose script fires an OS toast (notify-send, osascript, or a PowerShell toast) or returns terminalSequence with an OSC 9/777 desktop-notification escape for the terminal to render.
answers.rejected_alternative: A Stop hook: it fires when the turn ends, not when the run is blocked mid-turn waiting on an approval; Notification is the event that models 'waiting on the human'.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness emits the Notification event deterministically; the alert side effect is owned by the hook script.
answers.context_boundary: Runs outside the model context; message, title, and notification_type cross in via stdin and nothing crosses back to the model, since Notification hooks cannot block or modify anything.
answers.lifecycle: Fires every time Claude Code raises a matching notification in any session on that machine; stops when the hook entry is removed.
answers.failure_mode: Advisory and fails open: if the script errors or the desktop notification bus is unavailable, the run just sits blocked with no alert; the terminalSequence route additionally depends on the terminal emulator supporting the OSC sequence.
answers.version_caveat: terminalSequence requires v2.1.141+; the agent_needs_input and agent_completed matchers for background sessions require v2.1.198+ and only fire while agent view is open in a terminal.

answers.primary: Managed policy settings deployed fleet-wide via MDM (macOS com.anthropic.claudecode plist, Windows HKLM registry) or a system managed-settings.json (/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/, /etc/claude-code/, C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\), setting permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode to "disable" and optionally disableAutoMode.
answers.rejected_alternative: Putting disableBypassPermissionsMode in user or project settings.json: the key works from any scope, but a developer can simply edit those files, so only the managed scope satisfies 'cannot lift it from home directory or repo'.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness: managed settings sit at the top of the precedence order and cannot be overridden by user settings, project settings, or command-line arguments.
answers.context_boundary: Pure configuration evaluated at startup and on mode switches; nothing enters the model context beyond the refusal when bypass mode is attempted.
answers.lifecycle: Applied at every session start on every machine that carries the policy (SessionEnd even has a bypass_permissions_disabled reason); it stays in force until IT withdraws the policy.
answers.failure_mode: Fails open per machine that never received the profile or file: a laptop missing the policy has no restriction; mitigate with server-managed settings plus forceRemoteSettingsRefresh for fail-closed startup, and keep file-based policy in admin-only paths so users cannot edit it.
answers.version_caveat: The legacy C:\ProgramData\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json path is unsupported as of v2.1.75 (migrate to C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode); server-managed delivery and forceRemoteSettingsRefresh require the claude.ai admin console or a self-hosted Claude apps gateway.

answers.primary: A Stop command hook that verifies the test suite actually ran and passed during the turn and returns {"decision":"block","reason":...} otherwise, sending Claude back to work; pair it with a PostToolUse Bash hook that records test invocations and results to a session-keyed state file the Stop hook consults.
answers.rejected_alternative: A CLAUDE.md rule ('always run tests before finishing'): it is advisory and the stated problem is precisely that the model forgets; the built-in /goal prompt-based Stop hook is closer but is session-scoped and model-judged rather than deterministic.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness decides whether the turn may end; the model only receives the block reason and resumes working.
answers.context_boundary: The hook runs outside the context window, receiving stop_hook_active and last_assistant_message on stdin; its reason string crosses back into the conversation when it blocks.
answers.lifecycle: Fires every time the main agent tries to finish a turn; it must check stop_hook_active to avoid blocking on a condition that can never resolve, and Claude Code force-ends the turn after 8 consecutive blocks.
answers.failure_mode: Eventually fails open: after 8 consecutive blocks the harness overrides the hook, and a hook script error is non-blocking; a naive implementation that greps transcript_path can also miss the current turn because the transcript file is written asynchronously and lags.
answers.version_caveat: Stop decision control has no special gate; the background_tasks and session_crons inputs need v2.1.145+ if the hook wants to distinguish a genuinely finished turn from one paused for background work.

answers.primary: An explicit permissions.ask rule, "Bash(git push*)" (or "Bash(git push *)" plus the exact "Bash(git push)"), placed in managed or project settings: explicit ask rules force a prompt even in bypassPermissions and auto modes, so the human confirmation survives any approval configuration.
answers.rejected_alternative: A PreToolUse hook returning permissionDecision "ask": it works, but the declarative ask rule is the documented mechanism whose prompt survives bypassPermissions, and ask rules prompt even when a hook returns allow.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness: rules are evaluated deny, then ask, then allow, and neither an allow rule nor a permission mode can override a matching ask rule.
answers.context_boundary: Enforced at the Bash tool-call boundary in the main session and subagents; the command waits at the prompt and only the human's decision crosses.
answers.lifecycle: Evaluated on every Bash tool call for as long as the rule exists in settings, with live reload on edits; put it in managed settings if developers must not be able to remove it.
answers.failure_mode: Fails closed where no human can answer: in dontAsk mode the call is denied and in headless -p runs the prompt cannot be satisfied; the rule matches each subcommand of compound commands and past leading env assignments, but a push buried inside a script the agent runs (./deploy.sh) is not matched, so treat that as residual risk.
answers.version_caveat: No version gate: ask-rule survival in bypassPermissions is current documented behavior; the :* suffix and trailing-space wildcard forms are equivalent spellings.

answers.primary: PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure command hooks with matcher Bash (add PowerShell on Windows fleets), delivered through managed settings, appending timestamp, session_id, and tool_input.command from the stdin JSON to an append-only audit log.
answers.rejected_alternative: A PreToolUse hook: it fires before execution, so it records attempts including commands that were denied and never ran; the Post events record what actually executed and how it exited.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness fires the hooks on every Bash tool call; the model never mediates and never self-reports.
answers.context_boundary: The hook process runs outside the model context; the executed command line crosses in via stdin and goes to the log, and nothing returns to the conversation (silent exit 0).
answers.lifecycle: Runs on every Bash tool call in every session, including inside subagents where settings and managed hooks also fire; persists as long as the managed hook configuration is deployed.
answers.failure_mode: Advisory and fails open: a logging failure does not stop the command, and anything executed outside the Bash tool (an MCP server's own side effects, or grandchild commands a logged script spawns internally) is not captured as a separate line; deploy with allowManagedHooksOnly so developers cannot strip the hook.
answers.version_caveat: allowManagedHooksOnly is a managed-settings-only key; the prompt_id stdin field for correlating log lines with OpenTelemetry events requires v2.1.196+.

answers.primary: A PreToolUse command hook on Bash (if: "Bash(aws *)") that returns permissionDecision "deny" for any aws invocation, including each subcommand of compound commands, unless the command is exactly "aws s3 ls"; pair it with an allow rule "Bash(aws s3 ls)" so the approved call runs without prompting.
answers.rejected_alternative: Pure permission rules, deny "Bash(aws *)" plus allow "Bash(aws s3 ls)": deny is evaluated before allow, so the broad deny blocks the narrower allowed call too; a deny rule cannot carry an allowlist exception.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness: the hook's deny decision blocks the call before the permission prompt, and hook blocks take precedence over allow rules.
answers.context_boundary: The hook inspects the full command JSON outside the model context; only the deny reason crosses back so Claude can adjust course.
answers.lifecycle: Runs on every Bash tool call matching the aws pattern for the life of the settings entry; the if filter deliberately fails open on unparseable commands so the script still gets to inspect them.
answers.failure_mode: Degrades rather than breaks: if the hook script itself crashes, that is a non-blocking error and the call falls through to the normal permission flow, where non-allowlisted aws commands prompt instead of being refused outright; the script must itself check compound commands and $() substitutions rather than trusting the best-effort if filter.
answers.version_caveat: No significant version gate; the documented Bash if-matching table governs when the handler spawns, and the sample stdin-parsing pattern needs jq (or a PowerShell equivalent) on PATH.

answers.primary: OS-level sandboxing: sandbox.enabled true with filesystem.denyRead entries (or credentials.files deny entries) for ~/.aws/credentials and ~/.ssh; the Seatbelt/bubblewrap boundary applies to every process the Bash tool spawns, children of children included, and Read deny permission rules merge into the same boundary.
answers.rejected_alternative: Extending the PreToolUse hook or Read deny path rules: those bind only Claude's own tool calls and recognized file commands, not what a spawned Python process does with open(), which is exactly the reported gap.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness plus the operating system kernel: enforcement is physical process confinement, not behavioral compliance.
answers.context_boundary: Applies to the Bash tool's entire process tree in every session; denied bytes can never reach any spawned process, and therefore never reach any context window.
answers.lifecycle: The sandbox is applied to each Bash command execution while enabled in settings; it stops applying if sandboxing is disabled, the command is in excludedCommands, or the call uses the unsandboxed escape hatch.
answers.failure_mode: Fails open by default when the platform cannot sandbox (a warning is shown and commands run unsandboxed) unless failIfUnavailable is true; also close the escape hatches by setting allowUnsandboxedCommands false and keeping excludedCommands minimal, or the guarantee has holes.
answers.version_caveat: Sandboxing covers macOS, Linux, and WSL2 only (no native Windows) and defaults to off; credentials.files and credentials.envVars require v2.1.187+, and failIfUnavailable is intended for managed-settings deployments that need a hard gate.

answers.primary: Managed policy settings combining strictPluginOnlyCustomization: true (blocks skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers from user and project sources), force-enabled enabledPlugins from the IT marketplace, strictKnownMarketplaces plus blockedMarketplaces for source control, allowManagedHooksOnly and allowManagedMcpServersOnly as reinforcement, and disableSideloadFlags to close the CLI bypass.
answers.rejected_alternative: Distributing an approved plugin bundle by convention: plugins alone package the sanctioned components but do nothing to stop a developer adding ~/.claude/skills or committing .claude/agents into a repo; only managed-only settings lock those surfaces.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness: all of these are managed-settings-only keys that user and project scopes cannot set, and managed settings cannot be overridden by any other level.
answers.context_boundary: The gate operates at component discovery and load time across all sessions; blocked skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers never load, so nothing from them enters any context window.
answers.lifecycle: Enforced at session start and on settings reload on every machine carrying the policy; marketplace blocks are checked before download so blocked sources never touch disk; lasts until IT changes the policy.
answers.failure_mode: Fails open on any machine the policy never reached, and has coverage gaps if a key is omitted: without disableSideloadFlags a developer can pass --plugin-dir, --agents, or --mcp-config for a single run; blockedMarketplaces itself fails closed since blocked sources are rejected pre-download.
answers.version_caveat: disableSideloadFlags requires v2.1.193+; under allowManagedHooksOnly, plugin hook trust is granted by full plugin@marketplace ID, so a same-named plugin from another marketplace stays blocked; strictPluginOnlyCustomization also accepts an array to lock only selected surfaces.
